title: Computer Applications
description: ICSE Class IX Computer Applications: eleven chapters covering object-oriented concepts, language fundamentals, control flow and ethical computing, with Java 21 verified examples and practice questions.

syllabusBaselines.source: In-repo ICSE syllabus registry (src/lib/icseSyllabus.js, CLASS_IX_TOPICS) covering Object-oriented Programming Concepts, Language Fundamentals, Control Flow and Ethical & Social Computing.
syllabusBaselines.note: Syllabus structure is registered from the project's own canonical ICSE IX Computer Applications syllabus registry. All eleven chapters are authored to the boardprep schema, validated against the shared depth floors, and published with compiled-and-executed Java listings.

groups.title: Objects, Classes and the Java Environment

chapters.title: Introduction to Object Oriented Programming Concepts
chapters.blurb: Evolution of Java, the four OOP principles, the Java environment (JDK/JRE/JVM) and BlueJ — compilation and execution.

chapters.title: Elementary Concept of Objects and Classes
chapters.blurb: Classes as blueprints and objects as instances: attributes, methods, the new keyword and accessing members.

chapters.title: Identifiers and Literals
chapters.blurb: Tokens, identifier naming rules, keywords, variables and constants, literals, primitive data types and type conversion.

chapters.title: Operators in Java
chapters.blurb: Arithmetic, relational, logical, assignment, increment/decrement and ternary operators, with precedence and type compatibility.

chapters.title: Basic Structure of a Class in Java
chapters.blurb: Class declaration, the main method, System.out.println(), comments, and the compilation and execution process in BlueJ.

chapters.title: Data Processing in Java
chapters.blurb: Reading input with the Scanner class across data types and building simple data-processing programs with validation.

chapters.title: Mathematical Library Methods
chapters.blurb: The Math class: sqrt, pow, abs, ceil, floor, round and random, working with arguments and return values.

chapters.title: Conditional Statements in Java
chapters.blurb: if, else, else-if, nested if and switch-case with break and default for multi-way decisions.

chapters.title: Looping / Iterative Statements in Java
chapters.blurb: for, while and do-while loops, entry- versus exit-controlled iteration, and break and continue.

chapters.title: Nested for Loops
chapters.blurb: Outer and inner loops for row-and-column output, pattern programs and the discipline of the dry run.

chapters.title: Ethical Computing
chapters.blurb: Privacy, plagiarism, copyright and intellectual property, licences, and staying safe and responsible online.
